solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Like surefire investments good pal told Ed about (4-6)

indicatorNotes.about: "about" as in scattered about or turned about, so the letters are moved around into a new order

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
taken letter for letter

annotation.surface: A friend confides in Ed about some safe bets.
annotation.walkthrough: The G for good joins the fodder before the letters are rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: something gold-plated is guaranteed to pay off, as a surefire investment is.

entries.clue: Place for putting eco politician (5)

blocks.note: putting is the golf stroke, so this is the patch of short grass round the hole
a member of the environmentalist party

annotation.surface: Somewhere to install an environmentalist in office.
annotation.walkthrough: "Putting" reads as placing something, but it is the golf stroke: the putting green.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the golf green where players putt, and a Green, a member of an ecology party.

entries.clue: Veg, as a rule, is ground up in meat product (5,7)

indicatorNotes.ground up: meat that is ground up is minced into a new shape, so the letters are broken and remixed

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

annotation.surface: Vegetables normally get minced into a processed meat.
annotation.walkthrough: "Ground up" fits the sausage-making picture, which hides it as the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the answer is one kind of processed meat, the broad class the clue names.

entries.clue: Somewhat socialist US singer (4)

blocks.note: a pale shade of red, the colour of the left
the American pop singer who spells her name with an exclamation mark

annotation.surface: An American singer with mildly left-wing views.
annotation.walkthrough: Pink is a watered-down red, hence leaning left without going all the way.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: pink as slang for mildly left-wing, and P!nk, the US pop star.

entries.clue: Mail exposes “Barmy court” (6)

indicatorNotes.exposes: to expose is to strip the covering off, so each word loses its outer letters

blocks.note: BARMY with its outer letters B and Y removed
COURT with its outer letters C and T removed

annotation.surface: A tabloid headline ridiculing a court as mad.
annotation.walkthrough: "Mail" looks like the newspaper, but it is chain mail.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: chain mail is one kind of protective metal body covering worn in battle.

entries.clue: The Spanish explorer first to discover old legendary city (2,6)

indicatorNotes.first: "first to discover" is whatever comes first in discover, its opening letter

blocks.note: Spanish for "the"
Dora the Explorer, the children's cartoon character
first letter of discover
O is the standard abbreviation for old

annotation.surface: A Spanish explorer is first to find a fabled lost city.
annotation.walkthrough: The explorer is not a conquistador but the cartoon girl Dora.
annotation.definitionFit: A proper name: the fabled South American city of gold that Spanish explorers hunted for.

entries.clue: Elgar must have briefly upset composer (6,6)

indicatorNotes.briefly: a brief version is cut short, so the word loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.upset: something upset is knocked over and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
HAVE without its last letter

annotation.surface: Edward Elgar was bound to have annoyed a fellow composer.
annotation.walkthrough: One composer's name supplies letters for another's.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the Austrian late-Romantic symphonist is named only by his profession.

entries.clue: Spring, when Sergey goes cycling (6)

indicatorNotes.goes cycling: the letters are spun around like bicycle wheels, landing in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

annotation.surface: Springtime is when a man called Sergey takes his bike out.
annotation.walkthrough: "Spring" suggests the season; it is a source of water.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: an erupting jet of hot underground water is one kind of spring.

entries.clue: Denver uncovered French name for poison (7)

indicatorNotes.uncovered: with its cover taken off, the word loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: DENVER with its outer letters D and R removed
nom is French for name

annotation.surface: A Denver investigation reveals the French name of a toxin.
annotation.walkthrough: "Poison" looks like a noun but is a verb here.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: to put venom into something is to poison it.

entries.clue: Court status where both parties seek to gain advantage (5)

annotation.definition: Court status where both parties seek to gain advantage

blocks.note: the surface wants a law court; the setter means a tennis court and its score

blocks.clueFragment: where both parties seek to gain advantage
blocks.note: the parties are the two players, and advantage is the next score after it

annotation.surface: A lawsuit in which each side angles for the upper hand.
annotation.walkthrough: The court is a tennis court, the parties are the players, and "advantage" is a literal tennis score.
annotation.definitionFit: At 40-all in tennis, the score is called this, and the next point won gives advantage to that player.

entries.clue: Geeky dude involved in dinner date (4)

indicatorNotes.involved in: to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it, so the answer sits within the next words

blocks.note: dinNER Date

annotation.surface: A geek on a dinner date.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer spans the gap between the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a socially awkward enthusiast is a geek.

entries.clue: I hear you are in bistro cooking Mexican food (8)

indicatorNotes.I hear: what the setter hears is a sound, so write letters that sound like the phrase
indicatorNotes.in: one thing sits in the middle of another
indicatorNotes.cooking: cooking mixes and transforms ingredients, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: the letters U and R said together sound like "you are"
BISTRO rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone has heard you are at a bistro making tacos and the like.
annotation.walkthrough: The two letters go inside the jumbled bistro, right after its B.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: wrapped filled tortillas are one Mexican dish, and the plural matches.

entries.clue: Brightly coloured tail of indigo bird (8)

indicatorNotes.tail of: a word's tail is its back end, its final letter

blocks.note: blazing bright, the colour of fire
last letter of indigo

annotation.surface: A vivid bird with a deep blue tail.
annotation.walkthrough: "Brightly coloured" looks like a description of the bird, but it supplies the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the pink long-legged wader is one kind of bird.

entries.clue: Nobleman pursuing pony, initially one in valuable string (5)

indicatorNotes.pursuing: one who pursues follows behind, so the nobleman goes second
indicatorNotes.initially: what a word shows initially is its opening letter

blocks.note: first letter of pony
an earl is a British noble

annotation.surface: A lord chases a pony at the start of a race.
annotation.walkthrough: The valuable string is a necklace, and the answer is one bead on it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a necklace of precious beads is made of these, one at a time.

entries.clue: Season to pelt with shot? (6)

blocks.note: a verb: to flavour food with a spice
to spray a target with many small pellets

annotation.surface: Is it the season for shooting at things?
annotation.walkthrough: "Season" is a verb, as in seasoning food, not a time of year.
annotation.definitionFit: Two verb senses: to add a hot spice to food, and to riddle something with a scatter of shot.

entries.clue: One getting tanked up before going to work? (5)

annotation.definition: One getting tanked up before going to work?

blocks.note: the surface wants a drinker; the setter means someone strapping on air tanks
the work is done underwater once the tanks are on

annotation.surface: Someone who drinks heavily before starting a shift.
annotation.walkthrough: "Tanked up" means drunk, but here it means wearing scuba tanks.
annotation.definitionFit: A commercial or scuba worker fits air tanks before going down to do the job.

entries.clue: Frost seen in California peninsula (6)

indicatorNotes.seen in: what is seen in a place is inside it, so the first part sits within the second

blocks.note: the US postal abbreviation for California, outer part
rime is hoar frost, placed inside

annotation.surface: A cold snap has hit a Californian headland.
annotation.walkthrough: "Frost" is a noun for the ice, not the verb, and California is a state, not a place to picture.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the Black Sea landmass is one peninsula among many.

entries.clue: Letter might carry this page once ready in East Germany (8)

blocks.note: P is the standard abbreviation for page
the Ostmark was East Germany's currency, and ready is slang for cash

annotation.surface: A letter bearing a page once prepared in East Germany.
annotation.walkthrough: "Ready" means money, as in "the readies", and "once" signals a currency no longer used.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: posted letters bear this stamped cancellation over the stamp.

entries.clue: Doll that is leaving Sting? (4)

indicatorNotes.leaving: something leaving goes out of the word, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: the famous fashion doll
i.e. is the abbreviation for that is, and it is removed

annotation.surface: A doll departing to join Sting, the singer?
annotation.walkthrough: "Sting" looks like the musician, but it is a hurtful remark.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both nouns: a cutting remark, one that stings.

entries.clue: Coach regularly buys headgear for men (5)

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: a coach is a long-distance bus
the first and third letters of BuYs

annotation.surface: A sports coach routinely shops for his team's hats.
annotation.walkthrough: The men are soldiers: "men" in crosswords often means the ranks of an army.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the tall fur hat worn by hussars and other British regiments.

entries.clue: I’m responsible for this flipping endless dirge (4)

indicatorNotes.flipping: to flip something is to turn it over, so the letters read backwards
indicatorNotes.endless: without an end, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: DIRGE without its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone owning up to writing a dreadful mournful song.
annotation.walkthrough: "I" is the setter; "flipping" poses as a mild curse on the dirge.
annotation.definitionFit: A self-referential definition: the setter built the pattern of squares the solver is filling in.

entries.clue: Scottish nobleman’s broken leg at home (5)

indicatorNotes.broken: a broken word is smashed apart and its letters reassembled in a new order

blocks.note: LEG rearranged
being in means being at home

annotation.surface: A Scottish lord is laid up at home with a broken leg.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for "is", joining the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A title: the Earl of Elgin is a Scottish peer, best known for the marbles from the Parthenon.

entries.clue: Rolling Stones — blokes embodying R&B? (7)

indicatorNotes.embodying: to embody is to hold within one's body, so the blokes wrap round R&B

blocks.note: blokes are men, outer part
taken as printed without the ampersand, placed inside

annotation.surface: The Rolling Stones as men who personify rhythm and blues.
annotation.walkthrough: The band is a false lead: the definition means literal stones that roll.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition by description: small glass balls rolled in a children's game are stones that roll.

entries.clue: Carl and Del Boy organised game against neighbours (5,5)

indicatorNotes.organised: to organise is to arrange, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
taken letter for letter

annotation.surface: Two chancers set up a match with the team next door.
annotation.walkthrough: Del Boy is the wheeler-dealer of the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a sports match between rival teams from the same area.
